title: Dependency map of Parking.root_unimodal
root_label: unimodality by maximum displacement, as posed

units.label: alternating Taylor bounds for log(1+u)
units.description: For $u\ge0$ the Taylor polynomials of $\log(1+u)$ bound it alternately: the polynomial of even degree from below and the polynomial of odd degree from above.
units.lean:
Parking.log_one_add_taylor (n : ℕ) {u : ℝ} (hu : 0 ≤ u) :
  0 ≤ (-1) ^ n * (Real.log (1 + u) - ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, (-1) ^ i * u ^ (i + 1) / (↑i + 1))
units.statement:
For every natural number $n$ and every real number $u\ge0$,
$$0\ \le\ (-1)^n\Bigl(\log(1+u)-\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(-1)^i\frac{u^{i+1}}{i+1}\Bigr).$$
That is, with $T_n(u)=u-\frac{u^2}{2}+\dots+(-1)^{n-1}\frac{u^n}{n}$: $T_n(u)\le\log(1+u)$ for even $n$ and $\log(1+u)\le T_n(u)$ for odd $n$.

units.label: renewal sequence of a kernel
units.description: $u$ is the renewal sequence of the kernel $f$: $u_0=1$ and $u_n=\sum_{i=1}^{n}f_iu_{n-i}$ for every $n\ge1$.
units.lean: Parking.IsRenewal (f u : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop
units.statement:
Let $f=(f_i)_{i\ge0}$ and $u=(u_n)_{n\ge0}$ be sequences of real numbers. $u$ is *the renewal sequence of the kernel $f$* if
$$u_0=1\qquad\text{and}\qquad u_n=\sum_{i=1}^{n}f_i\,u_{n-i}\quad\text{for every } n\ge1.$$
The term $f_0$ does not occur.

units.label: log-convexity of the renewal sequence of a log-convex kernel
units.description: The renewal sequence of a positive log-convex kernel is log-convex: if $f_i>0$ and $f_{j+2}^2\le f_{j+1}f_{j+3}$, then $u_{n+1}^2\le u_nu_{n+2}$ for all $n$.
units.lean:
Parking.renewal_logConvex {f u : ℕ → ℝ} (hf : ∀ (i : ℕ), 1 ≤ i → 0 < f i)
  (hlc : ∀ (j : ℕ), f (j + 2) ^ 2 ≤ f (j + 1) * f (j + 3)) (hu : Parking.IsRenewal f u) (n : ℕ) :
  u (n + 1) ^ 2 ≤ u n * u (n + 2)
units.statement:
Let $f$ and $u$ be real sequences such that $u$ is the renewal sequence of the kernel $f$ (`Parking.IsRenewal`): $u_0=1$ and $u_n=\sum_{i=1}^{n}f_iu_{n-i}$ for $n\ge1$. Suppose that $f_i>0$ for every $i\ge1$ and that $f_{j+2}^2\le f_{j+1}f_{j+3}$ for every $j\ge0$, that is, that the sequence $f_1,f_2,f_3,\dots$ is log-convex. Then
$$u_{n+1}^2\le u_n\,u_{n+2}\qquad\text{for every } n\ge0.$$

units.label: resolvent representation of a renewal-type equation
units.description: If $G$ is the renewal sequence of a kernel $f$ and $v_s=\iota_s+\sum_{i=1}^{s}f_iv_{s-i}$ for all $s$, then $v$ is the convolution of $G$ with $\iota$: $v_s=\sum_{c=0}^{s}G_{s-c}\,\iota_c$.
units.lean:
Parking.resolvent {f G v ι : ℕ → ℝ} (hG : Parking.IsRenewal f G)
  (hι : ∀ (s : ℕ), v s = ι s + ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 s, f i * v (s - i)) (s : ℕ) :
  v s = ∑ c ∈ Finset.range (s + 1), G (s - c) * ι c
units.statement:
Let $f,G,v,\iota$ be sequences of real numbers. Suppose that $G$ is the renewal sequence of the kernel $f$ (`Parking.IsRenewal`): $G_0=1$ and $G_n=\sum_{i=1}^{n}f_iG_{n-i}$ for $n\ge1$. Suppose that for every $s\ge0$
$$v_s=\iota_s+\sum_{i=1}^{s}f_i\,v_{s-i}.$$
Then for every $s\ge0$
$$v_s=\sum_{c=0}^{s}G_{s-c}\,\iota_c.$$

units.label: Abel weights w_k(x)
units.description: The weights of Abel's binomial identity: $w_0(x) = 1$ and $w_k(x) = x\,(x+k)^{k-1}$ for $k \ge 1$, for a real number $x$.
units.lean: Parking.abelW (x : ℝ) (k : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For a real number $x$ and a natural number $k$,

$$w_k(x) = \begin{cases} 1, & k = 0, \\ x\,(x+k)^{k-1}, & k \ge 1. \end{cases}$$

units.label: Abel's binomial identity
units.description: Abel's binomial identity: $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k}\, w_k(x)\,(y-k)^{n-k} = (x+y)^n$ for real $x$, $y$, where $w_0(x) = 1$ and $w_k(x) = x\,(x+k)^{k-1}$ for $k \ge 1$.
units.lean:
Parking.abel_identity (n : ℕ) (x y : ℝ) :
  ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), ↑(n.choose k) * Parking.abelW x k * (y - ↑k) ^ (n - k) = (x + y) ^ n
units.statement:
For every natural number $n$ and all real numbers $x$ and $y$,

$$\sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k}\, w_k(x)\,(y-k)^{n-k} = (x+y)^n,$$

where $w_0(x) = 1$ and $w_k(x) = x\,(x+k)^{k-1}$ for $k \ge 1$ (`Parking.abelW`). Written out,

$$y^n + \sum_{k=1}^{n} \binom{n}{k}\, x\,(x+k)^{k-1}\,(y-k)^{n-k} = (x+y)^n .$$

The power with exponent $0$ is $1$; this concerns the term $k = n$, whose factor $(y-n)^0$ is $1$ also when $y = n$.

units.label: Cayley coefficients a_j
units.description: The Cayley coefficients $a_j = j^{j-1}/j!$ for $j \ge 1$, with $a_0 = 0$.
units.lean: Parking.cay (j : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For a natural number $j$, the Cayley coefficient $a_j$ is the real number defined by $a_0 = 0$ and

$$a_j = \frac{j^{\,j-1}}{j!} \qquad (j \ge 1).$$

units.label: convolution identity of the Cayley coefficients
units.description: The convolution identity of the Cayley coefficients $a_j = j^{j-1}/j!$ ($a_0 = 0$): $\sum_{\alpha=1}^{t-1} \alpha\, a_\alpha\, a_{t-\alpha} = (t-1)\, a_t$ for every $t \ge 0$.
units.lean:
Parking.cay_conv (t : ℕ) :
  ∑ α ∈ Finset.range t, ↑α * Parking.cay α * Parking.cay (t - α) = (↑t - 1) * Parking.cay t
units.statement:
For every natural number $t$,

$$\sum_{\alpha=0}^{t-1} \alpha\, a_\alpha\, a_{t-\alpha} = (t-1)\, a_t,$$

where $a_0 = 0$ and $a_j = j^{j-1}/j!$ for $j \ge 1$ (`Parking.cay`). The term $\alpha = 0$ is zero, so for $t \ge 2$ the sum runs over $1 \le \alpha \le t-1$. For $t = 0$ the sum is empty and the right-hand side is $(-1) \cdot a_0 = 0$; for $t = 1$ both sides are $0$.

units.label: log-convexity of the Cayley coefficients
units.description: The Cayley coefficients $a_j = j^{j-1}/j!$ are log-convex on $j \ge 1$, in the cross-multiplied form $a_{u+c}\,a_v \le a_u\,a_{v+c}$ for $1 \le u \le v$ and $c \ge 0$.
units.lean:
Parking.cay_logconvex {u v c : ℕ} (hu : 0 < u) (huv : u ≤ v) :
  Parking.cay (u + c) * Parking.cay v ≤ Parking.cay u * Parking.cay (v + c)
units.statement:
For all natural numbers $u$, $v$, $c$ with $1 \le u \le v$,

$$a_{u+c}\, a_v \le a_u\, a_{v+c},$$

where $a$ denotes the Cayley coefficients (`Parking.cay`).

units.label: ratio of consecutive Cayley coefficients
units.description: Consecutive Cayley coefficients $a_j = j^{j-1}/j!$ have the ratio $a_{j+1}/a_j = (1 + 1/j)^{j-1}$ for $j \ge 1$.
units.lean:
Parking.cay_ratio {j : ℕ} (hj : 0 < j) :
  Parking.cay (j + 1) = (1 + 1 / ↑j) ^ (j - 1) * Parking.cay j
units.statement:
For every natural number $j \ge 1$,

$$a_{j+1} = \Bigl(1 + \frac{1}{j}\Bigr)^{j-1} a_j,$$

where $a$ denotes the Cayley coefficients (`Parking.cay`).

units.label: normalised parking numbers c_n
units.description: The numbers $c_n = (n+1)^{n-1}/n!$ for $n \ge 0$: the number of parking functions of length $n$ divided by $n!$. They are the Cayley coefficients shifted by one, $c_n = a_{n+1}$.
units.lean: Parking.cc (n : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For a natural number $n$,

$$c_n = a_{n+1} = \frac{(n+1)^{n-1}}{n!},$$

where $a_j = j^{j-1}/j!$ is the Cayley coefficient (`Parking.cay`). In particular $c_0 = 1$.

units.label: recursion of the numbers c_n
units.description: The numbers $c_n = (n+1)^{n-1}/n!$ satisfy $(n+1)\,c_{n+1} = \sum_{j=0}^{n} (j+1)\,c_j\,c_{n-j}$ for every $n \ge 0$: the last-car recursion of parking functions without a displacement bound, divided by $n!$.
units.lean:
Parking.cc_rec (n : ℕ) :
  (↑n + 1) * Parking.cc (n + 1) =
    ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (↑j + 1) * Parking.cc j * Parking.cc (n - j)
units.statement:
For every natural number $n$,

$$(n+1)\,c_{n+1} = \sum_{j=0}^{n} (j+1)\,c_j\,c_{n-j},$$

where $c_n = (n+1)^{n-1}/n!$ (`Parking.cc`).

units.label: free prime kernel ε_m
units.description: The numbers $\varepsilon_m = (m-1)^{m-1}/m!$ for $m \ge 1$ (so $\varepsilon_1 = 1$), with $\varepsilon_0 = 0$.
units.lean: Parking.eps (m : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For a natural number $m$, the real number $\varepsilon_m$ is defined by $\varepsilon_0 = 0$ and

$$\varepsilon_m = \frac{(m-1)^{m-1}}{m!} \qquad (m \ge 1),$$

where $0^0 = 1$, so that $\varepsilon_1 = 1$.

units.label: the sequence n^n/n!
units.description: The sequence $\operatorname{ren}(n) = n^n/n!$ for $n \ge 0$, with $\operatorname{ren}(0) = 1$.
units.lean: Parking.ren (n : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For a natural number $n$,

$$\operatorname{ren}(n) = \frac{n^n}{n!},$$

where $0^0 = 1$, so that $\operatorname{ren}(0) = 1$.

units.label: total mass of the Borel law
units.description: The series $\sum_{j \ge 1} e^{-j} a_j$, with the Cayley coefficients $a_j = j^{j-1}/j!$, converges and has the sum $1$: the Borel law with parameter $1$ is a probability law, or, in other words, the tree function takes the value $1$ at its singularity $e^{-1}$.
units.lean: Parking.hasSum_borel : HasSum (fun j => Real.exp (-↑j) * Parking.cay j) 1
units.statement:
The series of nonnegative real numbers

$$\sum_{j \ge 0} e^{-j}\, a_j$$

converges, and its sum is $1$. Here $a_0 = 0$ and $a_j = j^{j-1}/j!$ for $j \ge 1$ (`Parking.cay`), so the term $j = 0$ is zero.

units.label: total mass of the kernel ε at the tilt 1/e
units.description: The series $\sum_{m \ge 1} e^{-m} \varepsilon_m$, with $\varepsilon_m = (m-1)^{m-1}/m!$, converges and has the sum $1 - e^{-1}$.
units.lean: Parking.hasSum_eps : HasSum (fun m => Real.exp (-↑m) * Parking.eps m) (1 - Real.exp (-1))
units.statement:
The series of nonnegative real numbers

$$\sum_{m \ge 0} e^{-m}\, \varepsilon_m$$

converges, and its sum is $1 - e^{-1}$. Here $\varepsilon_0 = 0$ and $\varepsilon_m = (m-1)^{m-1}/m!$ for $m \ge 1$, with $\varepsilon_1 = 1$ (`Parking.eps`), so the term $m = 0$ is zero.

units.label: the constant c_0 = 1/√(2π)
units.description: The constant $c_0 = 1/\sqrt{2\pi} \approx 0.39894$ of Stirling's formula.
units.lean: Parking.c0 : ℝ

units.label: Robbins' upper bound for the factorial
units.description: Robbins' upper bound for the factorial: $n! < \sqrt{2\pi n}\,(n/e)^n\, e^{1/(12n)}$ for every $n \ge 1$.
units.lean:
Parking.factorial_lt_robbins {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
  ↑n.factorial < √(2 * Real.pi * ↑n) * (↑n / Real.exp 1) ^ n * Real.exp (1 / (12 * ↑n))
units.statement:
For every natural number $n \ge 1$,

$$n! < \sqrt{2\pi n}\,\Bigl(\frac{n}{e}\Bigr)^{n} e^{1/(12n)}.$$

units.label: Poisson mass e^{-n} n^n/n!
units.description: The number $e^{-n} n^n/n!$ for $n \ge 0$: the probability that a Poisson variable with mean $n$ takes the value $n$. Its value at $n = 0$ is $1$.
units.lean: Parking.poissonMass (n : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For a natural number $n$, the Poisson mass at $n$ is

$$e^{-n}\,\frac{n^n}{n!} = e^{-n} \operatorname{ren}(n),$$

where $\operatorname{ren}(n) = n^n/n!$ with $0^0 = 1$ (`Parking.ren`).

units.label: lower Stirling bound of the Poisson mass
units.description: The Poisson mass is at least its Stirling approximation times $1 - \frac{1}{12n}$: $(1 - \frac{1}{12n})/\sqrt{2\pi n} \le e^{-n} n^n/n!$ for every $n \ge 1$.
units.lean:
Parking.poissonMass_ge {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
  (1 - 1 / (12 * ↑n)) / √(2 * Real.pi * ↑n) ≤ Parking.poissonMass n
units.statement:
For every natural number $n \ge 1$,

$$\Bigl(1 - \frac{1}{12n}\Bigr)\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi n}} \le e^{-n}\,\frac{n^n}{n!},$$

where the right-hand side is the Poisson mass of `Parking.poissonMass`.

units.label: upper Stirling bound of the Poisson mass
units.description: The Poisson mass is at most its Stirling approximation: $e^{-n} n^n/n! \le 1/\sqrt{2\pi n}$ for every $n \ge 1$.
units.lean: Parking.poissonMass_le {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) : Parking.poissonMass n ≤ 1 / √(2 * Real.pi * ↑n)
units.statement:
For every natural number $n \ge 1$,

$$e^{-n}\,\frac{n^n}{n!} \le \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi n}},$$

where the left-hand side is the Poisson mass of `Parking.poissonMass`.

units.label: the inverse series E = 1/P
units.description: The formal power series $E = 1/P$, the inverse of $P = \sum_{n \ge 0} c_n X^n$ with $c_n = (n+1)^{n-1}/n!$.
units.lean: Parking.TreeSeries.Eser : PowerSeries ℝ
units.statement: $E$ is the inverse, in the ring of formal power series over the real numbers, of the series $P = \sum_{n \ge 0} c_n X^n$ (`Parking.TreeSeries.Pser`), where $c_n = (n+1)^{n-1}/n!$ (`Parking.cc`). The inverse exists because the constant coefficient of $P$ is $c_0 = 1$.

units.label: the series P of the numbers c_n
units.description: The formal power series $P = \sum_{n \ge 0} c_n X^n$ with real coefficients, where $c_n = (n+1)^{n-1}/n!$.
units.lean: Parking.TreeSeries.Pser : PowerSeries ℝ
units.statement:
$P$ is the formal power series over the real numbers whose coefficient of $X^n$ is $c_n = (n+1)^{n-1}/n!$ (`Parking.cc`), for every $n \ge 0$:

$$P = \sum_{n \ge 0} c_n X^n = 1 + X + \tfrac{3}{2} X^2 + \tfrac{8}{3} X^3 + \cdots .$$

units.label: the tree series T
units.description: The tree series $T = X P = \sum_{j \ge 1} a_j X^j$, a formal power series with real coefficients, where $a_j = j^{j-1}/j!$ are the Cayley coefficients and $P = \sum_n c_n X^n$ with $c_n = a_{n+1}$.
units.lean: Parking.TreeSeries.Tser : PowerSeries ℝ
units.statement:
$T = X \cdot P$, where $P = \sum_{n \ge 0} c_n X^n$ is the series of the numbers $c_n = (n+1)^{n-1}/n!$ (`Parking.TreeSeries.Pser`). Its coefficient of $X^j$ is the Cayley coefficient $a_j$ (`Parking.cay`) for every $j \ge 0$ (`Parking.TreeSeries.coeff_Tser`):

$$T = \sum_{j \ge 1} a_j X^j = X + X^2 + \tfrac{3}{2} X^3 + \tfrac{8}{3} X^4 + \cdots .$$

units.label: coefficients of 1/P and of a quotient by P
units.description: For every real power series $f$, the coefficients of $f/P$ are $[X^n](E f) = f_n - \sum_{m=1}^{n} \varepsilon_m f_{n-m}$, where $P = \sum_n c_n X^n$, $c_n = (n+1)^{n-1}/n!$, $E = 1/P$ and $\varepsilon_m = (m-1)^{m-1}/m!$. Equivalently, $1/P = 1 - \sum_{m \ge 1} \varepsilon_m X^m$.
units.lean:
Parking.TreeSeries.coeff_Eser_mul (f : PowerSeries ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
  (PowerSeries.coeff n) (Parking.TreeSeries.Eser * f) =
    (PowerSeries.coeff n) f - ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, Parking.eps m * (PowerSeries.coeff (n - m)) f
units.statement:
Let $E = 1/P$ be the inverse of the series $P = \sum_{n \ge 0} c_n X^n$ (`Parking.TreeSeries.Eser`, `Parking.TreeSeries.Pser`). For every formal power series $f = \sum_j f_j X^j$ with real coefficients and every natural number $n$,

$$[X^n](E f) = f_n - \sum_{m=1}^{n} \varepsilon_m\, f_{n-m},$$

where $\varepsilon_m = (m-1)^{m-1}/m!$ for $m \ge 1$ (`Parking.eps`).

units.label: renewal equation of the numbers c_n
units.description: The numbers $c_n = (n+1)^{n-1}/n!$ satisfy the renewal equation $c_n = \sum_{m=1}^{n} \varepsilon_m\, c_{n-m}$ for $n \ge 1$, with the kernel $\varepsilon_m = (m-1)^{m-1}/m!$.
units.lean:
Parking.eps_conv {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
  ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, Parking.eps m * Parking.cc (n - m) = Parking.cc n
units.statement:
For every natural number $n \ge 1$,

$$\sum_{m=1}^{n} \varepsilon_m\, c_{n-m} = c_n,$$

where $c_n = (n+1)^{n-1}/n!$ (`Parking.cc`) and $\varepsilon_m = (m-1)^{m-1}/m!$ for $m \ge 1$, with $\varepsilon_1 = 1$ (`Parking.eps`).

units.label: log-convexity of the prime kernel
units.description: The prime kernel $\varepsilon_m = (m-1)^{m-1}/m!$ is log-convex: $\varepsilon_{m+1}^2 \le \varepsilon_m\,\varepsilon_{m+2}$ for every $m \ge 1$.
units.lean: Parking.eps_logconvex (n : ℕ) : Parking.eps (n + 2) ^ 2 ≤ Parking.eps (n + 1) * Parking.eps (n + 3)
units.statement: For every natural number $m \ge 1$, $\varepsilon_{m+1}^2 \le \varepsilon_m\,\varepsilon_{m+2}$, where $\varepsilon$ is the sequence of `Parking.eps`. In Lean, with $m = n + 1$: `eps (n + 2) ^ 2 ≤ eps (n + 1) * eps (n + 3)` for every natural number $n$.

units.label: step ratio of the prime kernel
units.description: The step ratio $g_m = \varepsilon_{m+1}/\varepsilon_m$ of the prime kernel $\varepsilon_m = (m-1)^{m-1}/m!$, defined by the explicit formula $g_1 = \frac12$, $g_m = \frac{m}{m+1}\bigl(1+\frac1{m-1}\bigr)^{m-1}$ for $m \ge 2$.
units.lean: Parking.gs (i : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For a natural number $m \ge 1$ put

$$g_1 = \frac12, \qquad g_m = \frac{m}{m+1}\Bigl(1+\frac1{m-1}\Bigr)^{m-1} \quad (m \ge 2).$$

The Lean function counts from zero: `gs i` is $g_{i+1}$, that is, `gs i` $= \frac{i+1}{i+2}\,(1+1/i)^{i}$ for every natural number $i$. For $i = 0$ the second factor is a zeroth power and equals $1$, which gives the value $\frac12$.

units.label: the extreme-column bound for renewal sequences
units.description: Let $G$ be the renewal sequence of a positive log-convex kernel $f$, let $v$ have nonnegative innovations with respect to $f$ up to time $\rho$, and let the weights $\theta$ be nonnegative and nondecreasing on $M,\dots,\rho$. Then $\bigl(\sum_{m=M}^{\rho}\theta_mf_mv_{\rho-m}\bigr)G_\rho \le \bigl(\sum_{m=M}^{\rho}\theta_mf_mG_{\rho-m}\bigr)v_\rho$.
units.lean:
Parking.extreme_column_le {f G v θ : ℕ → ℝ} {ρ M : ℕ} (hf : ∀ (i : ℕ), 1 ≤ i → 0 < f i)
  (hlc : ∀ (j : ℕ), f (j + 2) ^ 2 ≤ f (j + 1) * f (j + 3)) (hG : Parking.IsRenewal f G) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
  (hθ0 : 0 ≤ θ M) (hθ : ∀ (a b : ℕ), M ≤ a → a ≤ b → b ≤ ρ → θ a ≤ θ b)
  (hinn : ∀ s ≤ ρ, ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 s, f i * v (s - i) ≤ v s) :
  (∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc M ρ, θ m * (f m * v (ρ - m))) * G ρ ≤
    (∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc M ρ, θ m * (f m * G (ρ - m))) * v ρ

units.label: persistence on the far rows, beyond k + 0.47k
units.description: Let $k \ge 82$. If $d_{j,k} = b(j,k) - b(j,k-1)$ is positive on the rows $k + r_q \le j < k + r$, where $r_q \le k/3$ and $0.47k < r \le k-1$, then $d_{k+r,k} > 0$.
units.lean:
Parking.caseFar {k r rq : ℕ} (hk : 82 ≤ k) (h47 : 47 * k < 100 * r) (hr : r + 1 ≤ k)
  (h3 : 3 * rq ≤ k) (hpos : ∀ (j : ℕ), k + rq ≤ j → j < k + r → 0 < Parking.dq k j) :
  0 < Parking.dq k (k + r)
units.statement:
Let $b(n,\ell)$ be the number of parking functions of length $n$ with maximum displacement exactly $\ell$ (`Parking.b`), and $d_{j,k} = b(j,k) - b(j,k-1)$. Let $k \ge 82$, $r$ and $r_q$ be natural numbers with

$$47\,k < 100\,r, \qquad r + 1 \le k, \qquad 3\,r_q \le k.$$

Assume $d_{j,k} > 0$ for every $j$ with $k + r_q \le j < k + r$. Then $d_{k+r,\,k} > 0$.

The Lean statement is written with the normalised step $\delta_j = d_{j,k}/j!$ (`Parking.dq`, as `dq k j`), which has the same sign as $d_{j,k}$.

units.label: persistence of the sign along a column in the chain range
units.description: For $k \ge 2$ and $k + 1 \le n \le 2k-2$: if $b(n,k-1) < b(n,k)$, then $b(n+1,k-1) < b(n+1,k)$.
units.lean:
Parking.chain_column (k n : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (hn1 : k + 1 ≤ n) (hn2 : n ≤ 2 * k - 2)
  (h : Parking.b n (k - 1) < Parking.b n k) : Parking.b (n + 1) (k - 1) < Parking.b (n + 1) k
units.statement: Let $b(n,\ell)$ be the number of parking functions of length $n$ with maximum displacement exactly $\ell$ (`Parking.b`). Let $k \ge 2$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $k + 1 \le n \le 2k-2$. If $b(n,k-1) < b(n,k)$, then $b(n+1,k-1) < b(n+1,k)$.

units.label: persistence of the sign in the chain range, iterated
units.description: For $k \ge 2$ and $k + 1 \le m \le n \le 2k-1$: if $b(m,k-1) < b(m,k)$, then $b(n,k-1) < b(n,k)$.
units.lean:
Parking.chain_column_iter {k m n : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) (hm : k + 1 ≤ m) (hmn : m ≤ n)
  (hn : n ≤ 2 * k - 1) (h : Parking.b m (k - 1) < Parking.b m k) :
  Parking.b n (k - 1) < Parking.b n k
units.statement: Let $b(n,\ell)$ be the number of parking functions of length $n$ with maximum displacement exactly $\ell$ (`Parking.b`). Let $k \ge 2$, $m$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $k + 1 \le m \le n \le 2k-1$. If $b(m,k-1) < b(m,k)$, then $b(n,k-1) < b(n,k)$.

units.label: an early positive row in every column k ≥ 82
units.description: For every $k \ge 82$ there is a row $k + r$ with $1 \le r \le 0.27k$ at which $b(k+r,k-1) < b(k+r,k)$.
units.lean:

  ∃ r, 1 ≤ r ∧ 100 * r ≤ 27 * k ∧ 0 < Parking.dq k (k + r)
units.statement:
Let $b(n,\ell)$ be the number of parking functions of length $n$ with maximum displacement exactly $\ell$ (`Parking.b`), and $d_{n,k} = b(n,k) - b(n,k-1)$. For every natural number $k \ge 82$ there is a natural number $r$ with

$$1 \le r, \qquad 100\,r \le 27\,k, \qquad d_{k+r,\,k} > 0.$$

The Lean statement is written with the normalised step $\delta_n = d_{n,k}/n!$ (`Parking.dq`), which has the same sign.

units.label: persistence after an early crossing
units.description: Let $k \ge 82$ and $1 \le r_q \le k/3$. If $d_{j,k} = b(j,k) - b(j,k-1)$ is nonpositive on the rows $k \le j < k + r_q$ and positive at the row $k + r_q$, then $d_{n,k} > 0$ for every row $k + r_q \le n \le 2k-1$.
units.lean:
Parking.persist {k rq : ℕ} (hk : 82 ≤ k) (hrq : 1 ≤ rq) (h3 : 3 * rq ≤ k)
  (hneg : ∀ (j : ℕ), k ≤ j → j < k + rq → Parking.dq k j ≤ 0) (hq : 0 < Parking.dq k (k + rq))
  (n : ℕ) : k + rq ≤ n → n ≤ 2 * k - 1 → 0 < Parking.dq k n
units.statement:
Let $b(n,\ell)$ be the number of parking functions of length $n$ with maximum displacement exactly $\ell$ (`Parking.b`), and $d_{j,k} = b(j,k) - b(j,k-1)$. Let $k \ge 82$ and $r_q \ge 1$ be natural numbers with $3\,r_q \le k$. Assume

- $d_{j,k} \le 0$ for every $j$ with $k \le j < k + r_q$, and
- $d_{k+r_q,\,k} > 0$.

Then $d_{n,k} > 0$ for every $n$ with $k + r_q \le n \le 2k-1$.

The Lean statement is written with the normalised step $\delta_j = d_{j,k}/j!$ (`Parking.dq`, as `dq k j`), which has the same sign as $d_{j,k}$.

units.label: single crossing of a column k ≥ 82 in its chain range
units.description: Every column $k \ge 82$ has a row $q$ with $k+1 \le q \le k + 0.27k$ such that $b(j,k) \le b(j,k-1)$ for $k \le j < q$ and $b(n,k-1) < b(n,k)$ for $q \le n \le 2k-1$.

          ∀ (n : ℕ), q ≤ n → n ≤ 2 * k - 1 → 0 < Parking.dq k n

units.label: persistence on the near rows, up to k + 0.47k
units.description: Let $k \ge 42$. If $d_{j,k} = b(j,k) - b(j,k-1)$ is nonpositive on the rows $k \le j < q$ and positive on the rows $q \le j < n$, where $q = k + r_q$, $n = q + t$, $r_q, t \ge 1$ and $n - k \le 0.47k$, then $d_{n,k} > 0$.
units.lean:
Parking.caseA {k rq t : ℕ} (hk : 42 ≤ k) (hrq : 1 ≤ rq) (ht : 1 ≤ t) (h47 : 100 * (rq + t) ≤ 47 * k)
  (hneg : ∀ (j : ℕ), k ≤ j → j < k + rq → Parking.dq k j ≤ 0)
  (hpos : ∀ (j : ℕ), k + rq ≤ j → j < k + rq + t → 0 < Parking.dq k j) :
  0 < Parking.dq k (k + rq + t)
units.statement:
Let $b(n,\ell)$ be the number of parking functions of length $n$ with maximum displacement exactly $\ell$ (`Parking.b`), and $d_{j,k} = b(j,k) - b(j,k-1)$. Let $k \ge 42$, $r_q \ge 1$ and $t \ge 1$ be natural numbers with $100\,(r_q + t) \le 47\,k$. Assume

- $d_{j,k} \le 0$ for every $j$ with $k \le j < k + r_q$, and
- $d_{j,k} > 0$ for every $j$ with $k + r_q \le j < k + r_q + t$.

Then $d_{k+r_q+t,\,k} > 0$.

The Lean statement is written with the normalised step $\delta_j = d_{j,k}/j!$ (`Parking.dq`, as `dq k j`), which has the same sign as $d_{j,k}$.

units.label: the two-point condition of the near rows
units.description: For $k \ge 42$ the quantity $(k+\rho)\,\kappa_\rho$, with $\kappa_\rho = \varepsilon_\rho/\gamma_k^\rho$ the tilted kernel at the diagonal tilt, is nonincreasing in $\rho$ on the range $1 \le \rho \le 0.47k$.
units.lean:
Parking.Fk_anti {k a b : ℕ} (hk : 42 ≤ k) (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hab : a ≤ b) (hb : 100 * b ≤ 47 * k) :
  (↑k + ↑b) * Parking.kapx k b ≤ (↑k + ↑a) * Parking.kapx k a
units.statement:
Let $k \ge 42$ and let $a \le b$ be natural numbers with $1 \le a$ and $100\,b \le 47\,k$. Then

$$(k+b)\,\kappa_b \le (k+a)\,\kappa_a,$$

where $\kappa_m = x^m\varepsilon_m$ is the tilted kernel of `Parking.kapx`, $x = 1/\gamma_k$ is the diagonal tilt of `Parking.xk`, $\gamma_k = (1+1/k)^{k-2}$ and $\varepsilon_m = (m-1)^{m-1}/m!$.

units.label: the persistence inequality for abstract sequences
units.description: An abstract lower bound for a column $\delta$ at a row $n$. From the column equation at $n$, a diagonal lower bound $\gamma u_{j-1} - u_j \le \delta_j$ on the rows $k,\dots,n-1$, a kernel $\varepsilon$ with $\varepsilon_{m+1} \le \gamma\varepsilon_m$ for $m < \tau$, and $\delta \ge 0$ on the $\tau - 1$ rows before $n$: $\bigl(\frac2n - \varepsilon_\tau/\gamma^{\tau-1}\bigr)u_{n-1} + \sum_{m=\tau}^{n-k-1}(\gamma\varepsilon_m - \varepsilon_{m+1})\,u_{n-1-m} \le \delta_n$.

  (hstep : ∀ (m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → m < τ → ε (m + 1) ≤ γ * ε m)
  (hpos : ∀ (j : ℕ), n - τ + 1 ≤ j → j ≤ n - 1 → 0 ≤ δ j) :

      ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc τ (n - k - 1), (γ * ε m - ε (m + 1)) * u (n - 1 - m) ≤

units.label: the resolvent sequence of the frozen kernel
units.description: The sequence $G_s = e^{-s}\sum_{j=0}^{s}2^{-j}\,[X^s]\,X^jP^{j+1}$, where $P = \sum_n c_nX^n$ and $c_n = (n+1)^{n-1}/n!$. It is the renewal sequence of the frozen kernel.
units.lean: Parking.Gres (s : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For a natural number $s$,

$$G_s = e^{-s}\,H_s, \qquad H_s = \sum_{j=0}^{s}2^{-j}\,[X^s]\;X^jP(X)^{j+1},$$

where $P = \sum_{n\ge0}c_nX^n$ is the power series of `Parking.TreeSeries.Pser`, $c_n = (n+1)^{n-1}/n!$, and $H$ is the sequence of `Parking.Hres`. In Lean: `Gres s`.

units.label: the resolvent sequence is the renewal sequence of the frozen kernel
units.description: The sequence $G$ is the renewal sequence of the frozen kernel $f$: $G_0 = 1$ and $G_n = \sum_{i=1}^{n}f_iG_{n-i}$ for $n \ge 1$.
units.lean: Parking.Gres_isRenewal : Parking.IsRenewal Parking.fker Parking.Gres
units.statement:
Let $f$ be the frozen kernel of `Parking.fker` ($f_1 = \frac32e^{-1}$, $f_i = e^{-i}\varepsilon_i$ for $i\ge2$) and $G$ the sequence of `Parking.Gres`, $G_s = e^{-s}\sum_{j=0}^{s}2^{-j}[X^s]X^jP^{j+1}$. Then $G_0 = 1$ and, for every natural number $n \ge 1$,

$$G_n = \sum_{i=1}^{n} f_i\,G_{n-i}.$$

In Lean: `IsRenewal fker Gres`, with the predicate of `Parking.IsRenewal`.

units.label: lower bound of the resolvent sequence
units.description: For $s \ge 6$ the resolvent sequence of the frozen kernel satisfies $G_s \ge e\,\bigl(1-\frac1{12(s+1)}\bigr)\bigl(4-\frac{21}{s+1}\bigr)\big/\bigl((s+1)\sqrt{2\pi(s+1)}\bigr)$.
units.lean:
Parking.Gres_lower {s : ℕ} (hs : 6 ≤ s) :
  Real.exp 1 * ((1 - 1 / (12 * (↑s + 1))) / √(2 * Real.pi * (↑s + 1))) / (↑s + 1) *
      (4 - 21 / (↑s + 1)) ≤
    Parking.Gres s
units.statement:
For every natural number $s \ge 6$,

$$G_s \;\ge\; \frac{e}{s+1}\cdot\frac{1-\dfrac1{12(s+1)}}{\sqrt{2\pi(s+1)}}\cdot\Bigl(4-\frac{21}{s+1}\Bigr),$$

where $G$ is the sequence of `Parking.Gres`.

units.label: total mass of the resolvent sequence
units.description: Every partial sum of the resolvent sequence of the frozen kernel is at most $2e$: $\sum_{s<N}G_s \le 2e$.
units.lean: Parking.Gres_sum_le (N : ℕ) : ∑ s ∈ Finset.range N, Parking.Gres s ≤ 2 * Real.exp 1
units.statement:
For every natural number $N$,

$$\sum_{s=0}^{N-1} G_s \le 2e,$$

where $G$ is the sequence of `Parking.Gres`, the renewal sequence of the frozen kernel $f$ of `Parking.fker`.

units.label: the frozen kernel
units.description: The frozen kernel $f$: $f_1 = \frac32 e^{-1}$ and $f_i = e^{-i}\varepsilon_i$ for $i \ge 2$, where $\varepsilon_i = (i-1)^{i-1}/i!$. It is the prime kernel in the Borel scale with $\frac12e^{-1}$ added at the index $1$.
units.lean: Parking.fker (i : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For a natural number $i$,

$$f_i = e^{-i}\,\varepsilon_i + \begin{cases}\tfrac12 e^{-1} & \text{if } i = 1,\\ 0 & \text{otherwise,}\end{cases}$$

where $\varepsilon$ is the sequence of `Parking.eps`. Thus $f_0 = 0$, $f_1 = \frac32e^{-1}$, and $f_i = e^{-i}\varepsilon_i$ for $i \ge 2$. In Lean: `fker i`.

units.label: two-point persistence for abstract sequences
units.description: An abstract persistence statement. A sequence $\eta$ satisfies a column equation with feedback kernel $\kappa$ at a crossing row $q$ and at a later row $n$, is bounded below by the decrements of a nonnegative profile $U$ in between, is nonpositive before $q$ and positive on $[q, n)$; if $\kappa$ is positive, nonincreasing and log-convex in cross form and satisfies a condition comparing the two rows, then $\eta_n > 0$.
units.lean:

  (hcq : 0 ≤ cq) (hφq : 0 ≤ φq) (hφn : 0 < φn)
  (hCq :
    η (k + rq) =
      cq * U (k + rq - 1) + φq * η (k + rq - 1) + ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 rq, κ m * η (k + rq - m))
  (hCn :
    η (k + rq + t) =
      cn * U (k + rq + t - 1) + φn * η (k + rq + t - 1) +

  (hbase : η k = -U k) (hDg : ∀ (j : ℕ), k + 1 ≤ j → j + 1 ≤ k + rq + t → U (j - 1) - U j ≤ η j)
  (hU : ∀ (j : ℕ), 0 ≤ U j) (hκpos : ∀ (m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → m ≤ rq + t → 0 < κ m)
  (hκmono : ∀ (m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → m + 1 ≤ rq + t → κ (m + 1) ≤ κ m)
  (hκcross : ∀ (m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → m ≤ rq → κ (m + t) * κ rq ≤ κ (rq + t) * κ m)
  (hii : κ (rq + t) * cq ≤ κ rq * cn) (hneg : ∀ (j : ℕ), k ≤ j → j < k + rq → η j ≤ 0)
  (hpos : ∀ (j : ℕ), k + rq ≤ j → j < k + rq + t → 0 < η j) : 0 < η (k + rq + t)

units.label: column equation of a level
units.description: The column equation of the level $l\ge1$ on the rows $l+1\le n\le 2l+1$: $\beta^{(l)}_n=\frac1n z^{(l+1)}_{n-1}+\frac ln\beta^{(l)}_{n-1}+\sum_{m=1}^{n-l-1}\varepsilon_m\beta^{(l)}_{n-m}$, where $\beta^{(l)}_n=b(n,l)/n!$.
units.lean:
Parking.bq_L0 {l n : ℕ} (hl : 1 ≤ l) (hn1 : l + 1 ≤ n) (hn2 : n ≤ 2 * l + 1) :
  Parking.bq l n =
    Parking.zr (l + 1) (n - 1) / ↑n + ↑l / ↑n * Parking.bq l (n - 1) +
      ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n - l - 1), Parking.eps m * Parking.bq l (n - m)
units.statement:
Let $l\ge1$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $l+1\le n\le 2l+1$. Then
$$\beta^{(l)}_n=\frac{z^{(l+1)}_{n-1}}{n}+\frac{l}{n}\,\beta^{(l)}_{n-1}+\sum_{m=1}^{n-l-1}\varepsilon_m\,\beta^{(l)}_{n-m},$$
where $\beta^{(l)}_n=b(n,l)/n!$ (`Parking.bq`), $z^{(y)}_n=A(n,y-1)/n!$ (`Parking.zr`) and $\varepsilon_m=(m-1)^{m-1}/m!$ (`Parking.eps`).

units.label: normalised step of a column
units.description: The normalised step of the column $k$ in the row $n$: $\delta^{(k)}_n=\beta^{(k)}_n-\beta^{(k-1)}_n=(b(n,k)-b(n,k-1))/n!$.
units.lean: Parking.dq (k n : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For natural numbers $k\ge1$ and $n$,
$$\delta^{(k)}_n=\beta^{(k)}_n-\beta^{(k-1)}_n=\frac{b(n,k)-b(n,k-1)}{n!},$$
a real number, where $\beta^{(k)}_n=b(n,k)/n!$ (`Parking.bq`). When the column $k$ is fixed, the other records write $\delta_n$ for $\delta^{(k)}_n$. The Lean definition `dq k n` is also defined for $k=0$, where the subtraction of natural numbers gives $k-1=0$ and hence the value $0$.

units.label: initial value of the step of a column
units.description: The first nonzero value of the step of the column $k\ge2$: $\delta^{(k)}_k=-a_k/k$ with $a_k=k^{k-1}/k!$; in integers, $b(k,k)-b(k,k-1)=-k^{k-2}$.
units.lean: Parking.dq_base {k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) : Parking.dq k k = -(Parking.cay k / ↑k)
units.statement:
For every natural number $k\ge2$,
$$\delta^{(k)}_k=-\frac{a_k}{k},$$
where $\delta^{(k)}_n=(b(n,k)-b(n,k-1))/n!$ (`Parking.dq`) and $a_k=k^{k-1}/k!$ (`Parking.cay`).

units.label: column equation of the step
units.description: The column equation of the step of the column $k\ge2$ on the rows $k+1\le n\le 2k-1$: $\delta_n=\frac{k+1}{n}\delta_{n-1}+\frac2n\beta^{(k-1)}_{n-1}+\sum_{m=1}^{n-k}\varepsilon_m\delta_{n-m}$, where $\delta_n=(b(n,k)-b(n,k-1))/n!$.
units.lean:
Parking.dq_col {k n : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) (hn1 : k + 1 ≤ n) (hn2 : n ≤ 2 * k - 1) :
  Parking.dq k n =
    (↑k + 1) / ↑n * Parking.dq k (n - 1) + 2 / ↑n * Parking.bq (k - 1) (n - 1) +
      ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n - k), Parking.eps m * Parking.dq k (n - m)
units.statement:
Let $k\ge2$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $k+1\le n\le 2k-1$, and write $\delta_i=\delta^{(k)}_i=(b(i,k)-b(i,k-1))/i!$ (`Parking.dq`). Then
$$\delta_n=\frac{k+1}{n}\,\delta_{n-1}+\frac{2}{n}\,\beta^{(k-1)}_{n-1}+\sum_{m=1}^{n-k}\varepsilon_m\,\delta_{n-m},$$
where $\beta^{(k-1)}_i=b(i,k-1)/i!$ (`Parking.bq`) and $\varepsilon_m=(m-1)^{m-1}/m!$ (`Parking.eps`).

units.label: the factor of the diagonal lower bound
units.description: The factor $\gamma_k=(1+1/k)^{k-2}$ of the diagonal lower bound $\gamma_k\,\beta^{(k-1)}_{n-1}\le\beta^{(k)}_n$.
units.lean: Parking.gam (k : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For a natural number $k\ge2$,
$$\gamma_k=\Bigl(1+\frac1k\Bigr)^{k-2},$$
a real number. The Lean definition `gam k` is also defined for $k=0$ and $k=1$, where the exponent $k-2$ is the truncated difference $0$ (and $1/0=0$), so that $\gamma_0=\gamma_1=1$ there; for $k=1$ this differs from the ordinary reading $(1+1)^{-1}$.

units.label: tree curvature of a column
units.description: The tree curvature coefficients $\xi_t$ of the column $k$: $\xi_0=0$ and, for $t\ge1$, $t\,\xi_t=\min(t,k+1)\,z^{(k+1)}_{t-1}-2\min(t,k)\,z^{(k)}_{t-1}+\min(t,k-1)\,z^{(k-1)}_{t-1}$.
units.lean: Parking.xi (k t : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
Let $k\ge2$ be a natural number. The *tree curvature* of the column $k$ is the real sequence $\xi_t=\xi^{(k)}_t$, $t\ge0$, with $\xi_0=0$ and, for $t\ge1$,
$$\xi_t=\frac{1}{t}\Bigl(\min(t,k+1)\,z^{(k+1)}_{t-1}-2\,\min(t,k)\,z^{(k)}_{t-1}+\min(t,k-1)\,z^{(k-1)}_{t-1}\Bigr),$$
where $z^{(y)}_n=A(n,y-1)/n!$ (`Parking.zr`). The Lean definition `xi k t` is written for all natural numbers $k$, with $k-1$ the truncated difference; it is used only for $k\ge2$.

units.label: stochastic monotonicity along the diagonal
units.description: Stochastic monotonicity along the diagonal: for $y\ge1$ and every $n$, $z^{(y)}_n/c_n\le z^{(y+1)}_{n+1}/c_{n+1}$; that is, the probability that a uniform parking function of length $n$ has maximum displacement below $y$ does not decrease when $n$ and $y$ are both raised by one.
units.lean:
Parking.zr_diag_mono {y : ℕ} (hy : 1 ≤ y) (n : ℕ) :
  Parking.zr y n / Parking.cc n ≤ Parking.zr (y + 1) (n + 1) / Parking.cc (n + 1)
units.statement:
For all natural numbers $y\ge1$ and $n$,
$$\frac{z^{(y)}_n}{c_n}\;\le\;\frac{z^{(y+1)}_{n+1}}{c_{n+1}},$$
where $z^{(y)}_n=A(n,y-1)/n!$ (`Parking.zr`) and $c_n=(n+1)^{n-1}/n!$ (`Parking.cc`).

units.label: last-car recursion
units.description: The last-car recursion: the number $A(n+1,k)$ of parking functions of length $n+1$ with maximum displacement at most $k$ equals $\sum_{j=0}^{n}\min(j+1,k+1)\binom nj A(j,k)\,A(n-j,k)$.
units.lean:
Parking.A_succ (n k : ℕ) :
  Parking.A (n + 1) k =
    ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
      min (j + 1) (k + 1) * (n.choose j * (Parking.A j k * Parking.A (n - j) k))
units.statement:
For all natural numbers $n$ and $k$,
$$A(n+1,k)\;=\;\sum_{j=0}^{n}\min(j+1,\,k+1)\,\binom{n}{j}\,A(j,k)\,A(n-j,k).$$
Here $A(m,k)$ (`Parking.A`) is the number of parking functions of length $m$ whose maximum displacement is at most $k$; in particular $A(0,k)=1$ (`Parking.A_zero`).

units.label: the step as a second difference of A
units.description: For $k\ge2$ the step $b(n,k)-b(n,k-1)$ of the column $k$ in the row $n$ is the second difference $A(n,k)-2A(n,k-1)+A(n,k-2)$ of the cumulative counts in the bound $k$.
units.lean:
Parking.d_eq_A {k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) (n : ℕ) :
  ↑(Parking.b n k) - ↑(Parking.b n (k - 1)) =
    ↑(Parking.A n k) - 2 * ↑(Parking.A n (k - 1)) + ↑(Parking.A n (k - 2))
units.statement:
For all natural numbers $k\ge2$ and $n$,
$$b(n,k)-b(n,k-1)=A(n,k)-2A(n,k-1)+A(n,k-2)$$
as an identity of integers. Here $b(n,\ell)$ (`Parking.b`) is the number of parking functions of length $n$ with maximum displacement exactly $\ell$ and $A(n,k)$ (`Parking.A`) the number of those with maximum displacement at most $k$.

units.label: solution of the weighted last-car recursion
units.description: The predicate "$W$ solves the weighted last-car recursion with weight $\omega$": $W_0=1$ and $(n+1)W_{n+1}=\sum_{j=0}^{n}\omega(j+1)\,W_j\,W_{n-j}$ for all $n\ge0$, for real sequences $\omega$ and $W$.
units.lean: Parking.IsWSol (ω W : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop
units.statement:
Let $\omega$ and $W$ be sequences of real numbers indexed by the natural numbers. $W$ is a *solution of the weighted last-car recursion with weight $\omega$* if

- $W_0=1$, and
- for every $n\ge0$, $\;(n+1)\,W_{n+1}=\sum_{j=0}^{n}\omega(j+1)\,W_j\,W_{n-j}$.

units.label: single-chain formula, quotient form
units.description: Single-chain formula, quotient form. If $W$ solves the weighted last-car recursion with a weight that satisfies $\omega(t)=t$ for $1\le t\le k$, then for $1\le n\le 2k+1$ the quantity $W_n-\sum_{m=1}^{n}\varepsilon_mW_{n-m}$ is $0$ for $n\le k$ and $\frac{\omega(n)}{n}W_{n-1}-c_{n-1}$ for $n>k$.
units.lean:
Parking.IsWSol.ez {ω W : ℕ → ℝ} (h : Parking.IsWSol ω W) (k : ℕ)
  (hω : ∀ (t : ℕ), 1 ≤ t → t ≤ k → ω t = ↑t) {n : ℕ} (hn0 : 1 ≤ n) (hn : n ≤ 2 * k + 1) :
  W n - ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, Parking.eps m * W (n - m) =
    if n ≤ k then 0 else ω n / ↑n * W (n - 1) - Parking.cc (n - 1)
units.statement:
Let $\omega$ and $W$ be real sequences such that $W$ is a solution of the weighted last-car recursion with weight $\omega$ (`Parking.IsWSol`), and let $k$ be a natural number such that $\omega(t)=t$ for every $t$ with $1\le t\le k$. Then for every $n$ with $1\le n\le 2k+1$,
$$W_n-\sum_{m=1}^{n}\varepsilon_m\,W_{n-m}\;=\;\begin{cases}0,& n\le k,\\[2pt] \dfrac{\omega(n)}{n}\,W_{n-1}-c_{n-1},& n>k.\end{cases}$$
Here $c_n=(n+1)^{n-1}/n!$ (`Parking.cc`) and $\varepsilon_m=(m-1)^{m-1}/m!$ for $m\ge1$, with $\varepsilon_1=1$ (`Parking.eps`).

units.label: single-chain formula, forward form
units.description: Single-chain formula, forward form. If $W$ solves the weighted last-car recursion with a weight that satisfies $\omega(t)=t$ for $1\le t\le k$, then for $n\le 2k+1$: $c_n-W_n=\sum_{t=k+1}^{n}c_{n-t}\bigl(c_{t-1}-\frac{\omega(t)}{t}W_{t-1}\bigr)$.
units.lean:
Parking.IsWSol.fwd {ω W : ℕ → ℝ} (h : Parking.IsWSol ω W) (k : ℕ)
  (hω : ∀ (t : ℕ), 1 ≤ t → t ≤ k → ω t = ↑t) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≤ 2 * k + 1) :
  Parking.cc n - W n =
    ∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc (k + 1) n, Parking.cc (n - t) * (Parking.cc (t - 1) - ω t / ↑t * W (t - 1))
units.statement:
Let $\omega$ and $W$ be real sequences such that $W$ is a solution of the weighted last-car recursion with weight $\omega$ (`Parking.IsWSol`), and let $k$ be a natural number such that $\omega(t)=t$ for every $t$ with $1\le t\le k$. Then for every natural number $n\le 2k+1$,
$$c_n-W_n\;=\;\sum_{t=k+1}^{n}c_{n-t}\Bigl(c_{t-1}-\frac{\omega(t)}{t}\,W_{t-1}\Bigr),$$
where $c_n=(n+1)^{n-1}/n!$ (`Parking.cc`). For $n\le k$ the sum is empty and the statement is $W_n=c_n$.

units.label: normalised count of a column
units.description: The normalised count $\beta^{(k)}_n=b(n,k)/n!$: the number of parking functions of length $n$ with maximum displacement exactly $k$, divided by $n!$.
units.lean: Parking.bq (k n : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For natural numbers $k$ and $n$,
$$\beta^{(k)}_n=\frac{b(n,k)}{n!},$$
a real number, where $b(n,k)$ (`Parking.b`) is the number of parking functions of length $n$ whose maximum displacement is exactly $k$.

units.label: environment of a threshold
units.description: The normalised cumulative count $z^{(y)}_n=A(n,y-1)/n!$: the number of parking functions of length $n$ all of whose displacements are smaller than the threshold $y$, divided by $n!$.
units.lean: Parking.zr (y n : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For natural numbers $y\ge1$ and $n$,
$$z^{(y)}_n=\frac{A(n,y-1)}{n!},$$
a real number, where $A(n,k)$ (`Parking.A`) is the number of parking functions of length $n$ with maximum displacement at most $k$. The Lean definition `zr y n` is also defined for $y=0$, where the subtraction of natural numbers gives $y-1=0$, so that $z^{(0)}_n=z^{(1)}_n$.

units.label: the free range of a threshold
units.description: In the free range $n\le y$ of a threshold $y\ge1$ the normalised cumulative count equals the Cayley number: $z^{(y)}_n=A(n,y-1)/n!=c_n=(n+1)^{n-1}/n!$.
units.lean: Parking.zr_eq_cc {y n : ℕ} (hy : 1 ≤ y) (hn : n ≤ y) : Parking.zr y n = Parking.cc n
units.statement: Let $y\ge1$ and $n\le y$ be natural numbers. Then $z^{(y)}_n=c_n$, where $z^{(y)}_n=A(n,y-1)/n!$ (`Parking.zr`) and $c_n=(n+1)^{n-1}/n!$ (`Parking.cc`).

units.label: normalised last-car recursion
units.description: For a threshold $y\ge1$ the sequence $z^{(y)}_n=A(n,y-1)/n!$ solves the weighted last-car recursion with the weight $\omega(t)=\min(t,y)$: $z^{(y)}_0=1$ and $(n+1)z^{(y)}_{n+1}=\sum_{j=0}^{n}\min(j+1,y)\,z^{(y)}_jz^{(y)}_{n-j}$.
units.lean: Parking.zr_isWSol {y : ℕ} (hy : 1 ≤ y) : Parking.IsWSol (fun t => ↑(min t y)) (Parking.zr y)
units.statement:
Let $y\ge1$ be a natural number and $z^{(y)}_n=A(n,y-1)/n!$ (`Parking.zr`). Then $z^{(y)}$ is a solution of the weighted last-car recursion with the weight $\omega(t)=\min(t,y)$ in the sense of `Parking.IsWSol`; that is, $z^{(y)}_0=1$ and, for every $n\ge0$,
$$(n+1)\,z^{(y)}_{n+1}=\sum_{j=0}^{n}\min(j+1,y)\;z^{(y)}_j\,z^{(y)}_{n-j}.$$

units.label: crossing criterion in closed form
units.description: The crossing criterion with its five sums replaced by closed-form bounds: for $k\ge2$ and $2\le R\le k-1$, three explicit inequalities between elementary functions of $k$ and $R$ imply that $b(j,k)>b(j,k-1)$ in some row $j$ with $k<j\le k+R$.
units.lean:
Parking.cross_of_bounds {k R : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) (hR1 : 2 ≤ R) (hR2 : R ≤ k - 1)
  (hs : Parking.abar k * ↑R ≤ 6679 / 10000) (ht : 0 ≤ Parking.tlow k R)
  (h :
    (Parking.tup k R + Real.exp (-1) * Real.exp (Parking.abar k) * (↑R + 1) / (↑k + ↑R)) *
        (Parking.Hbar k R + 5 / ↑k * Parking.Gbar k R) <
      Real.exp (-1) * (↑R * (↑R + 1) / (↑k + ↑R) - 1 - Parking.Sbar k R - Parking.Ebar k R)) :
  ∃ j, k < j ∧ j ≤ k + R ∧ 0 < Parking.dq k j
units.statement:
Let $k\ge2$ and $R$ be natural numbers with $2\le R\le k-1$, and put $N=k+R$. Let $\bar a=5/(2k)$ (`Parking.abar`), and let $\bar S$, $\bar{\mathsf E}$, $\bar H$, $\bar G$, $\underline t$, $\bar t$ be the closed forms `Parking.Sbar`, `Parking.Ebar`, `Parking.Hbar`, `Parking.Gbar`, `Parking.tlow`, `Parking.tup`, evaluated at $(k,R)$. Suppose that
$$\bar a\,R\le\frac{6679}{10000},\qquad\underline t\ge0,$$
and
$$\Bigl(\bar t+e^{-1}e^{\bar a}\,\frac{R+1}{N}\Bigr)\Bigl(\bar H+\frac5k\,\bar G\Bigr)<e^{-1}\Bigl(\frac{R(R+1)}{N}-1-\bar S-\bar{\mathsf E}\Bigr).$$
Then there is a natural number $j$ with $k<j\le N$ and $d_{j,k}>0$, where $d_{j,k}=b(j,k)-b(j,k-1)$ (`Parking.b`).

units.label: truncated first moment of the kernel
units.description: The sum $S_R=\sum_{i=0}^{R-1}(ix)^i/i!$ for the diagonal tilt $x=1/\gamma_k$ of the column $k$; $x\,S_R$ is the first moment $\sum_{m=1}^{R}m\,\kappa_m$ of the tilted kernel masses up to $R$.
units.lean: Parking.SR (k R : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For natural numbers $k$ and $R$,
$$S_R=S_R(k)=\sum_{i=0}^{R-1}\frac{(i\,x)^i}{i!},$$
where $x$ is the diagonal tilt of the column $k$ (`Parking.xk`) and the term with $i=0$ is $1$.

units.label: weighted sum of the flow factors
units.description: The sum $\Sigma_\omega=\sum_{i=k+1}^{N-1}(i-k+1)\,\omega_i$, $N=k+R$, of the flow factors $\omega_i=1-i/((i+1)x\gamma_i)$ of the column $k$, each weighted by its distance from the row $k$ plus one.
units.lean: Parking.Somg (k R : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For natural numbers $k$ and $R$, with $N=k+R$,
$$\Sigma_\omega=\Sigma_\omega(k,R)=\sum_{i=k+1}^{N-1}(i-k+1)\,\omega_i,$$
where $\omega_i$ is the factor `Parking.omg` of the column $k$. For $R\le1$ the sum is empty and $\Sigma_\omega=0$.

units.label: crossing criterion
units.description: The crossing criterion: for a column $k\ge2$ and $1\le R\le k-1$, two explicit inequalities in $k$ and $R$ (the kernel deficit $\bar\kappa_R$ is nonnegative, and a product of two explicit sums is smaller than a third) imply that $b(j,k)>b(j,k-1)$ in some row $j$ with $k<j\le k+R$.
units.lean:
Parking.cross_criterion {k R : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) (hR1 : 1 ≤ R) (hR2 : R ≤ k - 1)
  (hκ : 0 ≤ Parking.kbar k R)
  (hK :
    (Parking.kbar k R + Parking.xk k * (↑R + 1) / (↑k + ↑R)) *
        (Parking.ecor k (k + R - 1) + Parking.Somg k R) <
      Parking.xk k * (↑R * (↑R + 1) / (↑k + ↑R) - 1 - Parking.SR k R - Parking.ecorSum k R)) :
  ∃ j, k < j ∧ j ≤ k + R ∧ 0 < Parking.dq k j
units.statement:
Let $k\ge2$ and $R$ be natural numbers with $1\le R\le k-1$, put $N=k+R$, and let $x=1/\gamma_k$ be the diagonal tilt of the column $k$ (`Parking.xk`). Let $\bar\kappa_R$ be the kernel deficit (`Parking.kbar`), $\mathsf e_{N-1}$ the tilt correction of the row $N-1$ (`Parking.ecor`), $\Sigma_\omega=\Sigma_\omega(k,R)$ the weighted sum of the flow factors (`Parking.Somg`), $S_R$ the sum `Parking.SR`, and $\mathsf E=\mathsf E(k,R)$ the accumulated tilt correction (`Parking.ecorSum`), all for the column $k$. Suppose that
$$\bar\kappa_R\ge0$$
and
$$\Bigl(\bar\kappa_R+\frac{x\,(R+1)}{N}\Bigr)\bigl(\mathsf e_{N-1}+\Sigma_\omega\bigr)<x\,\Bigl(\frac{R(R+1)}{N}-1-S_R-\mathsf E\Bigr).$$
Then there is a natural number $j$ with $k<j\le N$ and $d_{j,k}>0$, where $d_{j,k}=b(j,k)-b(j,k-1)$ and $b(n,\ell)$ is the number of parking functions of length $n$ with maximum displacement exactly $\ell$ (`Parking.b`).

units.label: tilt correction of a row
units.description: The correction $\mathsf e_j=(j-k+2)-\Pi_{j+1}/\pi_{j+1}$ of the column $k$: the amount by which the sum $\Pi_{j+1}=\pi_k+\dots+\pi_{j+1}$ of the weights, divided by its last term, falls short of its number of terms.
units.lean: Parking.ecor (k j : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For natural numbers $k$ and $j$,
$$\mathsf e_j=\mathsf e_j(k)=(j-k+2)-\frac{\Pi_{j+1}}{\pi_{j+1}},$$
where $\pi_n=x^na_n/n$ are the weights `Parking.pix` of the column $k$ and $\Pi_i=\sum_{n=k}^{i}\pi_n$ their partial sums `Parking.pixSum`. For $j\ge k$ this is
$$\mathsf e_j=\sum_{n=k}^{j+1}\Bigl(1-\frac{\pi_n}{\pi_{j+1}}\Bigr).$$

units.label: accumulated tilt correction
units.description: The sum $\mathsf E=\sum_{j=k}^{N-2}\mathsf e_j/(j+1)$, $N=k+R$, of the tilt corrections $\mathsf e_j$ of the column $k$ over the rows below the last two.
units.lean: Parking.ecorSum (k R : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For natural numbers $k\ge2$ and $R$, with $N=k+R$,
$$\mathsf E=\mathsf E(k,R)=\sum_{j=k}^{N-2}\frac{\mathsf e_j}{j+1},$$
where $\mathsf e_j=(j-k+2)-\Pi_{j+1}/\pi_{j+1}$ is the correction `Parking.ecor` of the column $k$. For $R\le1$ the sum is empty and $\mathsf E=0$.

units.label: tilted kernel masses
units.description: The tilted kernel masses $\kappa_m=x^m\varepsilon_m$ of the column $k$, where $x=1/\gamma_k$ is the diagonal tilt of the column and $\varepsilon_m=(m-1)^{m-1}/m!$.
units.lean: Parking.kapx (k m : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For natural numbers $k$ and $m$,
$$\kappa_m=\kappa_m(k)=x^m\,\varepsilon_m,$$
where $x$ is the diagonal tilt of the column $k$ (`Parking.xk`) and $\varepsilon_m$ is `Parking.eps`: $\varepsilon_m=(m-1)^{m-1}/m!$ for $m\ge1$ (so $\varepsilon_1=1$) and $\varepsilon_0=0$. In particular $\kappa_0=0$ and $\kappa_1=x$.

units.label: kernel deficit
units.description: The kernel deficit $\bar\kappa_M=1-x-\sum_{m=1}^{M}\kappa_m$ of the column $k$, where $x=1/\gamma_k$ is the diagonal tilt and $\kappa_m=x^m\varepsilon_m$ are the tilted kernel masses.
units.lean: Parking.kbar (k M : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For natural numbers $k$ and $M$,
$$\bar\kappa_M=\bar\kappa_M(k)=1-x-\sum_{m=1}^{M}\kappa_m,$$
where $x$ is the diagonal tilt of the column $k$ (`Parking.xk`) and $\kappa_m=x^m\varepsilon_m$ (`Parking.kapx`), with $\varepsilon_m=(m-1)^{m-1}/m!$ (`Parking.eps`). In particular $\bar\kappa_0=1-x$ and $\bar\kappa_1=1-2x$.

units.label: flow factor
units.description: The factor $\omega_i=1-i/((i+1)\,x\gamma_i)$ of the column $k$, where $x=1/\gamma_k$ is the diagonal tilt and $\gamma_i=(1+1/i)^{i-2}$; it bounds the diagonal increase of the cumulative proportion in the row $i$.
units.lean: Parking.omg (k i : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For natural numbers $k$ and $i$,
$$\omega_i=\omega_i(k)=1-\frac{i}{(i+1)\,x\,\gamma_i},$$
where $x$ is the diagonal tilt of the column $k$ (`Parking.xk`) and $\gamma_i$ is `Parking.gam`.

units.label: weights of the tilted source term
units.description: The weights $\pi_j=x^ja_j/j$ of the column $k$, where $x=1/\gamma_k$ is the diagonal tilt of the column and $a_j=j^{j-1}/j!$.
units.lean: Parking.pix (k j : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For natural numbers $k$ and $j\ge1$,
$$\pi_j=\pi_j(k)=\frac{x^j\,a_j}{j},$$
where $x$ is the diagonal tilt of the column $k$ (`Parking.xk`) and $a_j=j^{j-1}/j!$ (`Parking.cay`). The Lean definition also gives a value for $j=0$, namely $0$.

units.label: partial sums of the weights
units.description: The partial sums $\Pi_i=\sum_{n=k}^{i}\pi_n$ of the weights $\pi_n=x^na_n/n$ of the column $k$, starting at the index $k$.
units.lean: Parking.pixSum (k i : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For natural numbers $k$ and $i$,
$$\Pi_i=\Pi_i(k)=\sum_{n=k}^{i}\pi_n,$$
where $\pi_n=x^na_n/n$ are the weights `Parking.pix` of the column $k$ ($x$ is the diagonal tilt `Parking.xk`, $a_n=n^{n-1}/n!$ is `Parking.cay`). For $i<k$ the sum is empty and $\Pi_i=0$.

units.label: tilted profile at the diagonal tilt
units.description: The tilted profile $u_j=x^j\,\beta^{(k-1)}_j$ of the column $k$: the normalised counts $b(j,k-1)/j!$ of the column $k-1$, multiplied by the powers of the diagonal tilt $x=1/\gamma_k$ of the column $k$.
units.lean: Parking.profD (k j : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For natural numbers $k\ge1$ and $j$,
$$u_j=u_j(k)=x^j\,\beta^{(k-1)}_j,$$
where $x$ is the diagonal tilt of the column $k$ (`Parking.xk`) and $\beta^{(k-1)}_j=b(j,k-1)/j!$ (`Parking.bq`) is the number of parking functions of length $j$ with maximum displacement exactly $k-1$, divided by $j!$.

units.label: tilted step at the diagonal tilt
units.description: The tilted step $\eta_n=x^n\,\delta_n$ of the column $k$: the normalised step $\delta_n=(b(n,k)-b(n,k-1))/n!$ multiplied by the powers of the diagonal tilt $x=1/\gamma_k$.
units.lean: Parking.stepD (k n : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For natural numbers $k$ and $n$,
$$\eta_n=\eta_n(k)=x^n\,\delta_n,$$
where $x$ is the diagonal tilt of the column $k$ (`Parking.xk`) and $\delta_n=\beta^{(k)}_n-\beta^{(k-1)}_n=d_{n,k}/n!$ is the normalised step of the column $k$ in the row $n$ (`Parking.dq`), with $d_{n,k}=b(n,k)-b(n,k-1)$.

units.label: diagonal tilt of a column
units.description: The diagonal tilt $x=1/\gamma_k$ of the column $k$, where $\gamma_k=(1+1/k)^{k-2}$; for $k\ge2$ it is $x=(k/(k+1))^{k-2}$.
units.lean: Parking.xk (k : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
For a natural number $k$, the *diagonal tilt* of the column $k$ is the real number
$$x=x(k)=\frac1{\gamma_k},$$
where $\gamma_k$ is `Parking.gam`. For $k\ge2$ one has $\gamma_k=(1+1/k)^{k-2}$, and therefore $x=(k/(k+1))^{k-2}$.

units.label: crossing inside the strip
units.description: Every column $k\ge265$ is positive in some row $j>k$ with $25\,(j-k-1)^3\le121\,k^2$: there is a row $j$ with $k<j\le k+\lfloor(11k/5)^{2/3}\rfloor+1$ and $b(j,k)>b(j,k-1)$.
units.lean:
Parking.crossing_strip {k : ℕ} (hk : 265 ≤ k) :
  ∃ j, k < j ∧ 25 * (j - k - 1) ^ 3 ≤ 121 * k ^ 2 ∧ 0 < Parking.dq k j
units.statement:
Let $k\ge265$ be a natural number. Then there is a natural number $j$ with
$$k<j,\qquad25\,(j-k-1)^3\le121\,k^2,\qquad d_{j,k}>0,$$
where $d_{j,k}=b(j,k)-b(j,k-1)$ and $b(n,\ell)$ is the number of parking functions of length $n$ with maximum displacement exactly $\ell$ (`Parking.b`).

Since $25s^3\le121k^2$ is equivalent to $s\le(11k/5)^{2/3}$, the second condition says $j\le k+\varrho(k)+1$ with $\varrho(k)=\lfloor(11k/5)^{2/3}\rfloor$.

units.label: parking functions with maximum displacement at most k
units.description: $A(n,k)$ is the number of parking functions of length $n$ whose maximum displacement is at most $k$, that is, in which every car parks at most $k$ spots after the spot it prefers.
units.lean: Parking.A (n k : ℕ) : ℕ
units.statement:
For natural numbers $n$ and $k$,
$$A(n,k)=\#\{\alpha:\{0,\dots,n-1\}\to\{0,\dots,n-1\}\ :\ \alpha \text{ is a parking function and } M(\alpha)\le k\},$$
where $M(\alpha)$ is the maximum displacement of $\alpha$ (`Parking.maxDisp`), which is defined exactly when $\alpha$ is a parking function.

units.label: parking functions with maximum displacement exactly l
units.description: $b(n,\ell)$ is the number of parking functions of length $n$ whose maximum displacement is exactly $\ell$.
units.lean: Parking.b (n ℓ : ℕ) : ℕ
units.statement:
For natural numbers $n$ and $\ell$,
$$b(n,\ell)=\#\{\alpha:\{0,\dots,n-1\}\to\{0,\dots,n-1\}\ :\ \alpha \text{ is a parking function and } M(\alpha)=\ell\},$$
where $M(\alpha)$ is the maximum displacement of $\alpha$ (`Parking.maxDisp`), which is defined exactly when $\alpha$ is a parking function (`Parking.IsParkingFunction`).

units.label: displacements of the cars
units.description: The displacements of the cars: for a sequence of preferences $(a_1,\dots,a_m)$ and the sequence $(p_1,\dots,p_m)$ of the spots taken, the sequence of the differences $p_i-a_i$.
units.lean: Parking.dispList (prefs ps : List ℕ) : List ℕ
units.statement:
Let $(a_1,\dots,a_m)$ and $(p_1,\dots,p_{m'})$ be finite sequences of natural numbers, the preferences and the spots taken. Their sequence of displacements is
$$\bigl(\max(p_1-a_1,0),\ \dots,\ \max(p_r-a_r,0)\bigr),\qquad r=\min(m,m').$$
When the two sequences have the same length and $p_i\ge a_i$ for every $i$, as is the case for the spots taken in the parking process, this is $(p_1-a_1,\dots,p_m-a_m)$.

units.label: first free spot at or after a preference
units.description: The spot taken by a car with preference $a$ on a street with the spots $0,\dots,n-1$ when the spots of a set $U$ are occupied: the least spot $s\ge a$ of the street that is not in $U$, and no spot at all if there is none.
units.lean: Parking.firstFree (n : ℕ) (occ : Finset ℕ) (a : ℕ) : Option ℕ
units.statement:
Let $n$ and $a$ be natural numbers and let $U$ be a finite set of natural numbers. The street of length $n$ consists of the spots $0,1,\dots,n-1$. If there is a spot $s$ with $a\le s<n$ and $s\notin U$, then $\operatorname{first}_n(U,a)$ is the least such $s$. If there is none, that is, if every one of the spots $a,a+1,\dots,n-1$ belongs to $U$ (which includes the case $a\ge n$, where there is no such spot at all), then $\operatorname{first}_n(U,a)$ is undefined.

Spots are numbered from $0$ here; this is the convention of the Lean definition and is kept because the definition is a function of natural numbers.

units.label: maximum displacement
units.description: The maximum displacement $M(\alpha)$ of a parking function $\alpha$: the largest difference between the spot a car takes and the spot it prefers. It is undefined when $\alpha$ is not a parking function.
units.lean: Parking.maxDisp {n : ℕ} (α : Fin n → Fin n) : Option ℕ
units.statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $\alpha$ be a function from $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$ to itself. If $\alpha$ is a parking function, with the spots $\operatorname{pos}(\alpha)=(p_0,\dots,p_{n-1})$ taken by the cars (`Parking.positions`), then
$$M(\alpha)=\max\bigl(0,\ p_0-\alpha(0),\ \dots,\ p_{n-1}-\alpha(n-1)\bigr).$$
If $\alpha$ is not a parking function, $M(\alpha)$ is undefined.

For $n\ge1$ this is the maximum of the $n$ displacements $p_i-\alpha(i)\ge0$. For $n=0$ the only function is the empty one, it is a parking function, and $M=0$.

units.label: the parking process
units.description: The parking process: cars with given preferences arrive one after another at a street with the spots $0,\dots,n-1$, some of them already occupied, and each takes the first free spot at or after its preference. The result is the sequence of the spots taken, and it is undefined if some car cannot park.
units.lean: Parking.parkFrom (n : ℕ) : Finset ℕ → List ℕ → Option (List ℕ)
units.statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number, $U$ a finite set of natural numbers, and $(a_1,\dots,a_m)$ a finite sequence of natural numbers, $m\ge0$. Put $U_0=U$. For $i=1,\dots,m$ in turn, let $s_i=\operatorname{first}_n(U_{i-1},a_i)$ be the least spot $s$ with $a_i\le s<n$ and $s\notin U_{i-1}$ (`Parking.firstFree`), and put $U_i=U_{i-1}\cup\{s_i\}$. If every $s_i$ is defined, then $\operatorname{park}_n(U;a_1,\dots,a_m)=(s_1,\dots,s_m)$. If for some $i$ there is no such spot, then $\operatorname{park}_n(U;a_1,\dots,a_m)$ is undefined. For the empty sequence the result is the empty sequence.

The Lean definition is the equivalent recursion on the first car: $\operatorname{park}_n(U;\,)=()$, and for $m\ge1$, $\operatorname{park}_n(U;a_1,\dots,a_m)$ is defined exactly when $s_1=\operatorname{first}_n(U,a_1)$ and $(s_2,\dots,s_m)=\operatorname{park}_n(U\cup\{s_1\};a_2,\dots,a_m)$ are defined, and it is then $(s_1,s_2,\dots,s_m)$.

units.label: spots taken by the cars
units.description: The spots taken by the $n$ cars of a preference sequence $\alpha$ when they arrive in order at an empty street with the spots $0,\dots,n-1$; undefined if some car cannot park.
units.lean: Parking.positions {n : ℕ} (α : Fin n → Fin n) : Option (List ℕ)
units.statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $\alpha$ be a function from $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$ to itself. Then
$$\operatorname{pos}(\alpha)=\operatorname{park}_n(\emptyset;\alpha(0),\dots,\alpha(n-1)),$$
where $\operatorname{park}_n$ is the parking process (`Parking.parkFrom`) and $(\alpha(0),\dots,\alpha(n-1))$ is the preference sequence of $\alpha$ (`Parking.prefList`). Explicitly: the cars $0,1,\dots,n-1$ arrive in this order at the empty street with the spots $0,\dots,n-1$, and the car $i$ takes the least spot $s\ge\alpha(i)$, $s<n$, that no earlier car has taken. If every car finds such a spot, $\operatorname{pos}(\alpha)=(p_0,\dots,p_{n-1})$ is the sequence of the spots taken, $p_i$ being the spot of the car $i$. If some car finds none, $\operatorname{pos}(\alpha)$ is undefined.

units.label: preference sequence of a function

units.label: property K of the direct term
units.description: For $k\ge 7$ and $1\le\rho\le k-2$, the values $S_\rho(k-1)$, $S_\rho(k)$, $S_\rho(k+1)$ of the direct term of the first-layer recursion at the critical tilt $x_k$ form a triple with property K at $k$.
units.lean:
Parking.FirstLayer.Sdir_TK {k ρ n : ℕ} (hk : 7 ≤ k) (hρ : 1 ≤ ρ) (hn : ρ + n + 2 = k) :
  Parking.FirstLayer.TK (↑k) (Parking.FirstLayer.Sdir k ρ (k - 1)) (Parking.FirstLayer.Sdir k ρ k)
    (Parking.FirstLayer.Sdir k ρ (k + 1))
units.statement:
Let $k\ge 7$ and $\rho$ be natural numbers with $1\le\rho\le k-2$. Let $x_k=(k/(k+1))^{k-1}$ (`Parking.xcrit`), $\omega_n=c_nx_k^{\,n}$ with $c_n=(n+1)^{n-1}/n!$ (`Parking.ccT`), $Q_\rho(j)=\sum_{a=0}^{j}\omega_{\rho+a}\omega_{\rho+j-a}$ (`Parking.FirstLayer.pairT`) and
$$S_\rho(c)=x_k\,\omega_{\rho-1}\,\omega_c+\frac{x_k}{2}\cdot\frac{c+\rho+1}{c+\rho}\cdot Q_\rho(c-\rho-1)$$
(`Parking.FirstLayer.Sdir`). Then $\big(S_\rho(k-1),S_\rho(k),S_\rho(k+1)\big)$ has property K at $k$ (`Parking.FirstLayer.TK`): for every $\mu\ge 0$,
$$2e^{\mu/k}S_\rho(k)\le e^{\mu}S_\rho(k+1)+e^{-\mu}S_\rho(k-1).$$

The Lean statement names the number $n=k-\rho-2$ and assumes $\rho+n+2=k$.

units.label: property K of the diagonal triples of tilted masses in the first layer
units.description: For $k\ge 7$ and $0\le\rho\le k-2$, at the critical tilt $x_k$, the tilted masses $u^{(k-1)}_{k-1+\rho}$, $u^{(k)}_{k+\rho}$, $u^{(k+1)}_{k+1+\rho}$ of the thresholds $k-1$, $k$, $k+1$ at the sizes that exceed the threshold by $\rho$ form a triple with property K at $k$.

has property K at $k$ (`Parking.FirstLayer.TK`): for every real $\mu\ge 0$,
$$2\,e^{\mu/k}\,u^{(k)}_{k+\rho}\;\le\;e^{\mu}\,u^{(k+1)}_{k+1+\rho}+e^{-\mu}\,u^{(k-1)}_{k-1+\rho}.$$

units.statement:
Let $k\ge 7$ and $N$ be natural numbers with $k\le N\le 2k-2$. Let $x_k=(k/(k+1))^{k-1}$ (`Parking.xcrit`) and $u^{(y)}_M=z^{(y)}_M\,x_k^{\,M}$, where $z^{(y)}_M=A(M,y-1)/M!$ and $A(M,y-1)$ is the number of parking functions of length $M$ with all displacements smaller than $y$ (`Parking.zrT y (xcrit k) M`). $$u^{(k+1)}_{N+1}-2\,u^{(k)}_N+u^{(k-1)}_{N-1}\ \ge\ 0 .$$

Let $k\ge 3$ be a natural number, $x_k=(k/(k+1))^{k-1}$ (`Parking.xcrit`) and $\omega_n=c_nx_k^{\,n}$, $c_n=(n+1)^{n-1}/n!$ (`Parking.ccT` at the tilt $x_k$). Then the triple $(\omega_{k-1},\omega_k,\omega_{k+1})$ has property K at $k$ (`Parking.FirstLayer.TK`): for every real $\mu\ge 0$,
$$2\,e^{\mu/k}\,\omega_k\le e^{\mu}\,\omega_{k+1}+e^{-\mu}\,\omega_{k-1}.$$

units.label: tilted convexity of the Cayley masses below the top
units.description: At the critical tilt of a column $k\ge 3$, the tilted Cayley masses $\omega_n=c_nx_k^n$ satisfy $2e^{\mu/k}\omega_{j+1}\le e^{\mu}\omega_{j+2}+e^{-\mu}\omega_j$ for every $j$ with $j+2\le k$ and every real $\mu$.

Parking.FirstLayer.ccT_tilt_mid {k j : ℕ} (hk : 3 ≤ k) (hj : j + 2 ≤ k) (μ : ℝ) :

$$2\,e^{\mu/k}\,\omega_{j+1}\;\le\;e^{\mu}\,\omega_{j+2}+e^{-\mu}\,\omega_j .$$

units.label: property K of the pair sums
units.description: For $k\ge 3$ and $\rho+n+2=k$, the pair sums $Q_\rho(n)$, $Q_\rho(n+1)$, $Q_\rho(n+2)$ of tilted Cayley masses at the critical tilt $x_k$ form a triple with property K at $k$.

Parking.FirstLayer.pairT_TK {k ρ n : ℕ} (hk : 3 ≤ k) (hn : ρ + n + 2 = k) :
  Parking.FirstLayer.TK (↑k) (Parking.FirstLayer.pairT k ρ n) (Parking.FirstLayer.pairT k ρ (n + 1))
    (Parking.FirstLayer.pairT k ρ (n + 2))
units.statement:
Let $k\ge 3$, $\rho$, $n$ be natural numbers with $\rho+n+2=k$. Let $\omega_m=c_mx_k^{\,m}$ be the tilted Cayley masses at the critical tilt $x_k=(k/(k+1))^{k-1}$ (`Parking.ccT`, `Parking.xcrit`) and $Q_\rho(j)=\sum_{a=0}^{j}\omega_{\rho+a}\omega_{\rho+j-a}$ the pair sums (`Parking.FirstLayer.pairT`). Then the triple $\big(Q_\rho(n),\,Q_\rho(n+1),\,Q_\rho(n+2)\big)$ has property K at $k$ (`Parking.FirstLayer.TK`): for every $\mu\ge 0$,
$$2e^{\mu/k}\,Q_\rho(n+1)\le e^{\mu}\,Q_\rho(n+2)+e^{-\mu}\,Q_\rho(n).$$

units.label: property K of a triple
units.description: Property K at $k$ of a triple of real numbers $(a,b,c)$: the inequality $2e^{\mu/k}b\le e^{\mu}c+e^{-\mu}a$ holds for every real $\mu\ge 0$.

units.statement:

$$2\,e^{\mu/k}\,b\;\le\;e^{\mu}\,c+e^{-\mu}\,a\qquad\text{for every real }\mu\ge 0 .$$

units.label: property K under the factor (z+a)(z+b)/z
units.description: Property K at $k>1$ is preserved when the three values are multiplied by the values at $k-1$, $k$, $k+1$ of $z\mapsto(z+a)(z+b)/z$, where $a,b\ge 0$ and $ab\le k^2-1$, provided the middle value is nonnegative.

Parking.FirstLayer.TK.mul_prod {k a' b' c' a b : ℝ} (hk : 1 < k)
  (h : Parking.FirstLayer.TK k a' b' c') (hb' : 0 ≤ b') (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b)
  (hab : a * b ≤ k ^ 2 - 1) :
  Parking.FirstLayer.TK k ((k - 1 + a) * (k - 1 + b) / (k - 1) * a') ((k + a) * (k + b) / k * b')

units.statement:

$$\Big(\frac{(k-1+a)(k-1+b)}{k-1}\,a',\ \ \frac{(k+a)(k+b)}{k}\,b',\ \ \frac{(k+1+a)(k+1+b)}{k+1}\,c'\Big)$$
has property K at $k$.

units.label: property K under the factor (z+α)/(z+β)
units.description: Property K at $k>1$ is preserved when the three values are multiplied by the values at $k-1$, $k$, $k+1$ of $z\mapsto(z+\alpha)/(z+\beta)$, $0\le\alpha\le\beta$, provided the middle value is nonnegative.

Parking.FirstLayer.TK.mul_ratio {k a b c α β : ℝ} (hk : 1 < k) (h : Parking.FirstLayer.TK k a b c)
  (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hαβ : α ≤ β) :

    ((k + 1 + α) / (k + 1 + β) * c)
units.statement:
Let $k>1$ be real, let $(a,b,c)$ have property K at $k$ (`Parking.FirstLayer.TK`) with $b\ge 0$, and let $0\le\alpha\le\beta$ be real. Then the triple
$$\Big(\frac{k-1+\alpha}{k-1+\beta}\,a,\ \ \frac{k+\alpha}{k+\beta}\,b,\ \ \frac{k+1+\alpha}{k+1+\beta}\,c\Big)$$
has property K at $k$.

units.label: direct part of the last-car recursion in the first layer
units.description: The direct part $D(c,P)=\sum_{a=0}^{c-P}\min(P+a+1,c)\,\omega_{P+a}\,\omega_{c-a}$ of the last-car recursion at the size $c+P+1$ and the threshold $c$: the terms in which both pieces have size at most $c$.
units.lean: Parking.FirstLayer.direct (k c P : ℕ) : ℝ
units.statement:
Let $k$, $c$, $P$ be natural numbers with $P\le c$, $x_k=(k/(k+1))^{k-1}$ (`Parking.xcrit`) and $\omega_n=c_nx_k^{\,n}$, where $c_n=(n+1)^{n-1}/n!$ (`Parking.ccT` at the tilt $x_k$). The direct part is
$$D(c,P)=\sum_{a=0}^{c-P}\min(P+a+1,\,c)\;\omega_{P+a}\;\omega_{c-a}.$$

units.description: For a threshold $c\ge 1$ and $P\le c$, at the tilt $x_k$: $(c+P+1)\,u^{(c)}_{c+P+1}=x_k\big(\sum_{i<P}(c+i+1)\,\omega_i\,u^{(c)}_{c+P-i}+D(c,P)\big)$, where $u^{(c)}$ is the tilted environment of the threshold $c$, $\omega$ the tilted Cayley masses and $D(c,P)$ the direct part.
units.lean:
Parking.FirstLayer.zrT_split {k c P : ℕ} (hc : 1 ≤ c) (hP : P ≤ c) :
  (↑c + ↑P + 1) * Parking.zrT c (Parking.xcrit k) (c + P + 1) =
    Parking.xcrit k *
      (∑ i ∈ Finset.range P,
          (↑c + ↑i + 1) * Parking.ccT (Parking.xcrit k) i *
            Parking.zrT c (Parking.xcrit k) (c + (P - i)) +
        Parking.FirstLayer.direct k c P)
units.statement:
Let $k$, $c$, $P$ be natural numbers with $c\ge 1$ and $P\le c$. Let $x_k=(k/(k+1))^{k-1}$ (`Parking.xcrit`), $\omega_n=c_nx_k^{\,n}$ with $c_n=(n+1)^{n-1}/n!$ (`Parking.ccT`), and $u^{(c)}_N=z^{(c)}_N\,x_k^{\,N}$, where $z^{(c)}_N=A(N,c-1)/N!$ and $A(N,c-1)$ is the number of parking functions of length $N$ all of whose displacements are smaller than $c$ (`Parking.zrT c (xcrit k) N`). units.label: order of the kernel weights on the rows before the crossing
units.description: For a column $k\ge 2$, a row $q\le k+\frac{27}{100}k$, a row $n\ge 2k$ and every $j<q$: $\kappa_{n-j}\,(2k-1)\le\kappa_{n-q+1}\,\Psi'(j)$, where $\kappa$ is the prime kernel of the threshold $k$ at the critical tilt and $\Psi'(j)=\max(j,2k-1)$.

units.statement: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers with $n\ge 17$, $k\ge 1$ and $2k\le n$. Then $b(n,k-1)\le b(n,k)$.
